t: #2323 Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs II
o: Each worker takes exactly one job and finishes it in ceil(job / worker) days; all run in parallel, so the answer is the maximum completion time over the assignment. Example 1 pairs jobs [5,2,4] with workers [1,7,5] achieving max 2. The optimal assignment pairs the smallest job with the smallest worker, second-smallest with second-smallest, etc. (exchange argument: swapping to restore this order never increases the max), so sort both arrays and take the max ratio.
k: Optimal matching: sort jobs and workers ascending and pair by rank — provable by an exchange argument.
Answer = max over i of ceil(jobs[i] / workers[i]) after sorting.

a.n: Approach 1: Sort Both and Pair by Rank
a.i: Sorting both arrays and matching by index minimizes the maximum ceiling-division time. Any inversion (big job with small worker while a smaller job has a bigger worker) can be swapped without raising the max, so the sorted pairing is optimal.
s: Sort jobs ascending and workers ascending.
Compute t_i = ceil(jobs[i] / workers[i]) for each i.
a.t: O(n log n) — two sorts dominate; the pairing scan is linear.

w: One approach is genuinely optimal here; a brute force over permutations (O(n!)) only serves as intuition. Pitfall: integer division without the ceiling adjustment ((j + w - 1) // w), and forgetting the answer is the MAX, not the sum. Follow-up: if workers could take multiple jobs, this becomes scheduling on unrelated machines — NP-hard, needing binary search + greedy checks.
